Name: Exodilla Starcrasher
Information:
**Exodilla**

Pods of exodilla remain scattered in the universe, living nomadic lives as scavengers among the stars. These groups are not unlike the more savage lizardfolk of Somnus Domina, who see other species as prey to be hunted or invaders to be defended against.

**Exodilla Starcrasher**

Occasionally an exodilla is born with a genetic mutation that causes it to develop extreme amounts of muscle, harder scales, and it grows to an imposing size. These exodilla have reduced mental abilities and their bodies are more traditionally lizard-like. They are commonly friendly to other exodilla, and so are made into guardians of their pods or used as weapons in raids. Sometimes a temperamental starcrasher may take control of its own pod like a wild beast, demanding food and entertainment in exchange for mercy.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The exodilla makes one Bite attack and one Tail attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage plus 5 (1d8) acid damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 23 (3d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Acid Wave (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: The exodilla breathes a 60-foot-long, 10-foot-wide line of acid originating from itself. Each creature in range must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 50 (9d10) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success.

bonus_actions.name: Spine Dash (2/Rest)
bonus_actions.description: The exodilla curls into a ball and rolls 30 feet in a straight line (or 60 feet in a zero-gravity environment), aiming to end their movement in an unoccupied space it can see. Creatures riding it are safely contained inside the ball with it, harmlessly moving with it. Each Large or smaller creature the exodilla passes through is subjected to a Tail attack by the exodilla. If it collides with a Huge or larger creature, the exodilla stops moving.
